Pass 1: on a, B goes to D and A goes to B. (D, B) is already marked, so (B, A) is distinguishable: mark it.
Pass 1: on a, C goes to D and B goes to B. (D, B) is already marked, so (C, B) is distinguishable: mark it.
Pass 1: on a, E goes to D and D goes to B. (D, B) is already marked, so (E, D) is distinguishable: mark it.
Pass 2 marks nothing new, so stop. Unmarked pairs are equivalent. Merge {A, C}.

reversed.note: Several final states, so new start q_s with λ-moves to each of them.

steps.text: Start with the λ-closure of the NFA start state: λ-closure({q0}) = {q0, q1, q2, q3, q4, q5, q8, q9, q13, q15}. Call it A. It is the DFA start state.
Mark A. move(A, 0) = {q7, q12}, and its λ-closure is {q7, q11, q12, q15}. This set is new, so it becomes state B.
Mark A. move(A, 1) = {q6}, and its λ-closure is {q1, q2, q3, q4, q5, q6, q8, q9, q10, q13, q15}. This set is new, so it becomes state C.
Mark B. move(B, 0) = ∅. The empty set becomes the trap state ∅.
Mark B. move(B, 1) = {q14}, and its λ-closure is {q1, q2, q3, q4, q5, q8, q9, q10, q13, q14, q15}. This set is new, so it becomes state D.
Mark C. move(C, 0) = {q7, q12}, and its λ-closure is {q7, q11, q12, q15}. That set is already state B.
Mark C. move(C, 1) = {q6}, and its λ-closure is {q1, q2, q3, q4, q5, q6, q8, q9, q10, q13, q15}. That set is already state C.
Mark ∅. move(∅, 0) = ∅. That set is already state ∅.
Mark ∅. move(∅, 1) = ∅. That set is already state ∅.
Mark D. move(D, 0) = {q7, q12}, and its λ-closure is {q7, q11, q12, q15}. That set is already state B.
Mark D. move(D, 1) = {q6}, and its λ-closure is {q1, q2, q3, q4, q5, q6, q8, q9, q10, q13, q15}. That set is already state C.
Every state is marked, so stop. Final states are the sets that contain an NFA final state: A, B, C, D.
Write every pair of states once (the lower triangle). A pair gets × when the two states are distinguishable.
Pass 0: a final and a non-final state are always distinguishable (λ tells them apart). Mark (∅, A), (∅, B), (∅, C), (D, ∅).
Pass 1: on 0, B goes to ∅ and A goes to B. (∅, B) is already marked, so (B, A) is distinguishable: mark it.
Pass 1: on 0, C goes to ∅ and B goes to B. (∅, B) is already marked, so (C, B) is distinguishable: mark it.
Pass 1: on 0, D goes to ∅ and B goes to B. (∅, B) is already marked, so (D, B) is distinguishable: mark it.
Pass 2 marks nothing new, so stop. Unmarked pairs are equivalent. Merge {A, C, D}.
